text: Everything in Chapters 4 through 6 described what a practice should do. ITIL 4 is deliberately silent on how an organization actually executes that day to day — it's a framework, not software. In practice, most mid-size and large organizations run these practices inside an IT service management platform, and ServiceNow is the one you'll see most often in ITIL-aligned enterprises. It doesn't change what the practices are; it gives them a shared system of record.

ServiceNow's module names read almost like a translation of the practice list. Incident Management and Problem Management are literally named that. Change Management is ServiceNow's actual module name for what ITIL 4 calls change enablement, carrying the risk assessment and CAB approval routing from Lesson 16. Request Management, built on the Service Catalog, turns service requests into a browsable, orderable list. Knowledge Management stores the articles agents and self-service users search first. Service level management shows up as SLA definitions attached directly to records.

Underneath almost all of this sits the CMDB, the Configuration Management Database — a structured map of every configuration item and how it relates to the others and to the services it supports. This is the platform's version of the service configuration management practice from Lesson 23. Log an incident against an application, and the CMDB is what shows every other configuration item that application actually depends on.

The service desk practice isn't one screen. The Agent Workspace is where IT staff work tickets, with CMDB relationships, knowledge articles, and SLA countdowns all visible together in one dense view. The Employee or Service Portal is what everyone else sees — a self-service storefront for submitting requests, searching knowledge articles, and checking status on something already logged, without ever touching the agent side. Same underlying records, two purpose-built experiences.

Nothing here required clicking anything, because this course has been building the vocabulary that makes a platform like ServiceNow make sense the first time you open it. The next course in this path, ServiceNow Platform Fundamentals, is where hands-on navigation finally starts.
